definition_zh: 带来；带（人）来；引起、导致；使达到（某状态）
definition_en: to carry something or someone to the place where the speaker is, to cause something to happen, or to make something reach a state
core_image: 手里提着东西、朝你走过来的人
scene: 妹妹从厨房端着一盘水果，走到客厅放到桌上。 My sister brought a plate of fruit to the living room.
sceneCN: 这里 bring 是「带来」（第 1 个义项：把东西带到说话者所在的地方）；句意为我妹妹把一盘水果端到了客厅。

pos.zh: 动词：带来；带（人）来；引起；使达到

derivatives.zh: 由 bring 加 -er 构成，义为「带来者；送来的人」
由 up 与 bringing 组合而成，义为「抚养；教养」

senses.title: To carry something here
senses.definition: to carry or take something to the place where the speaker is
senses.definitionCN: 把东西搬到说话者所在的地方
senses.example: My sister brought a plate of fruit to the living room.
senses.exampleCN: 我妹妹把一盘水果端到了客厅。
senses.why: Old English bringan meant to carry something along, and the direction toward the speaker is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bringan 意为把东西一路搬来，朝说话者所在方向的意思已经包含在词里。

senses.title: To take a person along
senses.definition: to take someone with you to a place
senses.definitionCN: 把某人一起带到某个地方
senses.example: He brought a friend to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他带了一位朋友来参加聚会。
senses.why: The same carrying motion applies to people, who are led along instead of lifted.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「带过来」的动作也适用于人，只不过人是被领着走，而不是被提起来。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或出现
senses.example: The new road brought many visitors to the town.
senses.exampleCN: 新公路给小镇带来了许多游客。
senses.why: What is carried in arrives as a result, so the word came to mean producing an effect.
senses.whyCN: 被带进来的东西会带来结果，于是这个词也引申为产生某种影响。

senses.title: To make something reach a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to reach a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物达到某种特定状态
senses.example: The rain brought the game to an end.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨使比赛提前结束了。
senses.why: A thing is carried all the way to a new state, as if that state were a destination.
senses.whyCN: 某物被一路带到新的状态，仿佛那个状态就是一个目的地。

intro.en: Bring is an old verb for carrying something toward the speaker, and its senses grew toward cause and result.
intro.cn: bring 是一个表示「把东西朝说话者搬来」的古老动词，词义逐步扩展到原因与结果。

items.en: Bringan meant to carry something along to a place.
items.cn: bringan 意为把某物一路搬到某处。

items.en: German bringen and Dutch brengen keep the same meaning.
items.cn: 德语 bringen 与荷兰语 brengen 保持相同的意思。

items.en: The verb kept its shape as bring, with brought as the past tense.
items.cn: 这个动词保持 bring 的词形，过去式为 brought。

items.en: What a person carries in also produces an effect, so bring gained the sense of causing.
items.cn: 人带进来的东西也会产生效果，于是 bring 获得了「引起」的意思。

items.en: Today bring covers carrying things and people, causing changes and reaching a state.
items.cn: 今天 bring 覆盖带物、带人、引起变化与达到某种状态。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about carrying and causing.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与携带、引起有关的词。

root: bring 来自古英语 bringan，意为把东西一路搬到某处，与德语 bringen、荷兰语 brengen 同源，方向始终指向说话者所在之处。这个词的用法从搬动物品扩展到带人同行；被带进来的东西会产生结果，于是又引申为「引起」；某物被一路带到新的状态，则引申为「使达到」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bring grow from one picture: a person walking toward you with something in hand.
sensesIntro.cn: bring 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一个人手里提着东西朝你走来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking toward you carrying something
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人提着东西朝你走来

branches.en: THE OBJECT: carrying a thing to the speaker is the first sense.
branches.cn: 物品线：把东西搬到说话者这里是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same motion leads a friend along.
branches.cn: 人物线：同样的动作也能把朋友带来。

branches.en: THE EFFECT: what arrives also produces a result.
branches.cn: 效果线：带进来的东西也会产生结果。

branches.en: THE STATE: a thing is carried all the way to a new condition.
branches.cn: 状态线：某物被一路带到新的状况。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL: things and people share one direction toward the speaker.
branches.cn: 到达线：物与人共享同一个朝说话者的方向。

definition_zh: 协议；同意；一致；合同
definition_en: a deal between people or countries, or the state of sharing an opinion
core_image: 双方在文件上签字握手
scene: 会谈结束后，双方在文件上签字并握手。 The two countries signed an agreement.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 是「协议」（第 1 个义项：双方达成的约定）；句意为两国签署了一项协议。

pos.zh: 名词：协议；同意；一致；合同

senses.title: A written deal
senses.definition: an arrangement that two sides have accepted
senses.definitionCN: 双方都接受的安排
senses.example: The two schools signed an agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两所学校签署了一项协议。
senses.why: Agree plus -ment names the result of agreeing, and a signed result is an agreement.
senses.whyCN: agree 加 -ment 指谈成的结果，签下来的结果就是协议。

senses.title: The state of agreeing
senses.definition: the fact of sharing the same view
senses.definitionCN: 看法相同这件事
senses.example: There was general agreement on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 大家对这项计划普遍表示同意。
senses.why: The same ending also names the state of sharing a view.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也可以指看法相同的状态，就是同意。

senses.title: Matching between accounts
senses.definition: the state of two accounts being the same
senses.definitionCN: 两种说法彼此相同
senses.example: There is agreement between the two stories.
senses.exampleCN: 两种说法之间是一致的。
senses.why: The state of being of one mind was applied to accounts, giving the sense of matching.
senses.whyCN: 把「意见合一」用在两种说法上，就得到一致、相符。

items.cn: agreer 意为同意或相合。

items.en: Today it covers contracts, treaties and grammar rules.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖合同、条约与语法规则。

definition_zh: 玻璃；玻璃杯；一杯之量；眼镜（复数）
definition_en: a hard transparent material, a drinking cup made of it, the amount it holds, or eyeglasses in the plural
core_image: 透明的硬片：能看穿却摸不着
scene: 厨房里，一杯牛奶被碰倒，透明的碎片溅到了地上。 He picked up the broken glass from the kitchen floor.
sceneCN: 这里 glass 是「玻璃杯」（第 2 个义项：玻璃制的饮水容器）；句意为他从厨房地板上拾起碎玻璃杯。

pos.zh: 玻璃；玻璃杯；一杯之量；眼镜
给……装玻璃；把……做成玻璃状

derivatives.zh: 由 glass 加 -y 构成，义为「玻璃般的；呆滞的」
glass 与 ware 的复合词，义为「玻璃器皿」
eye 与 glass 的复合词，义为「镜片；眼镜」

senses.title: The hard transparent material
senses.definition: a hard, transparent substance used for windows, bottles and mirrors
senses.definitionCN: 用于窗、瓶、镜的坚硬透明材料
senses.example: The window glass shattered into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 窗玻璃碎成了小块。
senses.why: The core image is a clear, see-through solid, so the first sense is the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是透明可看穿的固体，所以第一义项就是材料本身。

senses.title: A drinking cup made of glass
senses.definition: a container for drinking, made of glass
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃制的饮用容器
senses.example: He picked up the broken glass from the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他从厨房地板上拾起碎玻璃杯。
senses.why: The material is shaped into a cup, so the maker of cups borrows the material's name.
senses.whyCN: 材料被制成杯子，杯具便沿用材料的名字。

senses.title: The amount a glass holds
senses.definition: the quantity that a glass contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只玻璃杯所容的量
senses.example: She drank two glasses of juice at breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早餐喝了两杯果汁。
senses.why: The cup measures what it carries, so the container becomes a unit of drink.
senses.whyCN: 杯子量出所盛之物，容器便成了计量单位。

senses.title: Eyeglasses
senses.definition: two lenses in a frame worn to see better, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 戴在眼前帮助视力的双镜片，用复数
senses.example: Grandpa put on his glasses to read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷戴上眼镜读那封信。
senses.why: Two glass lenses sit before the eyes, so the pair of lenses takes the plural of the material.
senses.whyCN: 两片玻璃镜片置于眼前，成对的镜片便沿用材料的复数形式。

senses.title: To fit with glass or become glassy
senses.definition: to put glass into a frame, or to become glassy and dull-eyed
senses.definitionCN: 给框架装玻璃，或眼神变得呆滞发直
senses.example: The workers glassed the porch last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们去年春天给门廊装了玻璃。
senses.why: The material name turns into a verb when glass is put into something or eyes look like it.
senses.whyCN: 当玻璃被装进某物、或眼神像玻璃时，材料名便转为动词。

intro.en: Glass runs back to a Germanic word for the shining material itself.
intro.cn: glass 直接追溯到日耳曼语中指这种闪亮材料的词。

items.en: The reconstructed root glazam meant the transparent shining substance.
items.cn: 重构词根 glazam 意为透明的闪光物质。

items.en: Old English glæs meant glass, already the material and the cup.
items.cn: 古英语 glæs 意为玻璃，已兼指材料与杯具。

items.en: Norse gler, meaning shining glass, is a relative from the same family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gler 意为闪亮的玻璃，是同族的亲属词。

items.en: Middle English glas settled the form and added the drink-measure use.
items.cn: 中古英语 glas 固定了词形，并增加了计饮量的用法。

items.en: Modern English spelled it glass and grew the eyeglasses and verb senses.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 glass，并发展出眼镜义与动词用法。

note.en: The words below echo glass in sound or share its transparent world.
note.cn: 以下词与 glass 音近，或同属透明器物的世界。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「班级；类别」，与 glass 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Like glass in look; dull or smooth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「玻璃般的；呆滞的」，由 glass 直接派生。

entries.definition: A yellow metal alloy; rhymes with glass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄铜」，与 glass 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: A small open container for drinking, often with a handle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杯子」，常带柄，不一定透明。

entries.definition: Clear colourless glass of fine quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水晶玻璃」，指高品质透明玻璃。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass for seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「镜片」，与 glasses 的核心部分相关。

normal.cn: glassy 形容有光泽却无神采的眼神。

abstract.cn: 想象雨水滑过窗玻璃，你透过它望着街道。

abstract.en: See a drinking glass turn empty, leaving a ring of water on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃杯被喝空，桌上留下一圈水痕。

abstract.en: Think of shattered pieces catching sunlight on the floor.

sensesIntro.en: Glass moves from the material to the cup, the measure, the lenses and finally the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: glass 从材料延伸到杯子、计量、镜片，最后转为动词。

core.cn: 核心意象：可以一眼看穿的透明固体

branches.en: the material and its fitting
branches.cn: 玻璃材料与安装动作

branches.cn: 玻璃杯与杯中之量

branches.cn: 呆滞发直的眼神

intro.en: Glass is a Germanic base noun; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: glass 是日耳曼基础名词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitrum 意为玻璃，是平行的拉丁词，并非 glass 的来源。

definition_zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的；孤零零的
definition_en: unhappy because one lacks company; (of a place) far from others and rarely visited; standing apart with nothing similar nearby
core_image: 深夜的公交站牌下，只有一个人影和一条长长的影子
scene: 雪停了，屋檐下的灯还亮着，屋里只有一个人。 She felt lonely in the new flat, even though the street outside was full of noise.
sceneCN: 这里是「因缺少陪伴而难受」（第 1 个义项：独自一人时感到寂寞）；句意为虽然外面的街道很吵，她在新公寓里仍然觉得寂寞。

pos.zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的

derivatives.zh: lonely 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「孤独；寂寞」
由词干 lone 加 -er 构成，义为「独来独往的人」
lonely 的词干，由 alone 截短而来，义为「单独的；无伴的」
由 alone 加 -ness 构成，义为「独自一人的状态」

senses.title: Sad because one has no company
senses.definition: unhappy because one lacks company or close contact with other people
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少陪伴或与他人的亲近接触而难受
senses.example: He grew lonely after his closest friends moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 最亲近的朋友搬走以后，他变得孤独起来。
senses.why: Lone means being just one, and -ly turns that state into a feeling; the pain comes from having nobody to answer you.
senses.whyCN: lone 意为「只有一个人」，-ly 把这种状态变成一种感受；难受的根源是身边没有人回应自己。

senses.title: Remote and rarely visited
senses.definition: of a place: far from other places, with few people passing through
senses.definitionCN: 指地方远离别处，很少有人经过
senses.example: The farm stood on a lonely stretch of the coast road.
senses.exampleCN: 那座农场孤零零地立在海岸公路的一段上。
senses.why: A place that is one by itself, far from any neighbour, borrows the human word for isolation and turns it into a description of distance.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方独自存在、离任何邻里都远，于是借用了写人的「孤立」一词，把它变成对距离的描述。

senses.title: Standing apart with nothing similar nearby
senses.titleCN: 孤零零的；旁边没有同样的东西
senses.definition: of a thing: standing alone, separated from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 指物体单独立着，和同类分开
senses.example: A lonely tree stood at the top of the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶上立着一棵孤零零的树。
senses.why: From people to places and then to objects, the same shape repeats: one thing, no companion, a visible gap around it.
senses.whyCN: 从人扩展到地方，再扩展到物体，重复的是同一个形状：只有一样东西，没有同伴，四周留着一圈看得见的空。

intro.en: Lonely is built from lone, a shortened form of alone, which began as the Old English phrase for all one; the word for one lies underneath all of it.
intro.cn: lonely 由 lone 加后缀构成，而 lone 是 alone 的截短形式；alone 最初是古英语中「全部为一」的说法，底下站着的是表示「一」的词。

items.en: The English word one and Latin unus both descend from a shared Indo-European form for a single unit.
items.cn: 英语的 one 与拉丁语 unus 都来自印欧语系中表示「一个单位」的同一个形式。

items.en: An meant one, and al, meaning all, was joined to it, so al an said all one, that is, entirely by oneself.
items.cn: ān 意为「一」，表示「全部」的 al 加在前面，al an 就是「全部为一」，也就是完完全全只有自己。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, alone, and speakers later clipped off the first syllable to make lone.
items.cn: 这个短语后来写成一个词 alone，再往后说话的人省掉了开头音节，得到了 lone。

items.en: Adding -ly to lone made lonely, which describes not the fact of being alone but the state of feeling it.
items.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 得到 lonely，它描述的不是独处的事实，而是独处带来的状态。

items.en: Modern English uses lonely for people, for remote places and for single objects standing apart from their kind.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lonely 写人、写偏僻的地方，也写单独立着、和同类分开的物体。

note.en: The look-alike group traces the family back to the word for one; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of isolation and emptiness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「一」这个词把整族词串起来；近义组收表示孤立与空寂的形容词。

entries.definition: Single or without company, used mainly before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的、无伴的，多用在名词前。

entries.definition: By oneself, with nobody else present.
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人，没有其他人在场。

entries.definition: The state or feeling of being lonely.
A person who chooses to spend time alone.
A chiefly American word close in meaning to lonely.
entries.definitionCN: 主要用于美国英语，意思接近 lonely。

entries.definition: Done alone, or living alone by choice.
entries.definitionCN: 独自做的，或自愿独居的。

entries.definition: Cut off from other people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 与其他人或地方隔绝的。

entries.definition: Empty because everyone has left.
entries.definitionCN: 因为人都离开而空荡的。

entries.definition: Far away from towns and other people.

normalIntro.en: Lonely rests on the old phrase for all one, so the word measures how far a person is from any other voice.
normalIntro.cn: lonely 立在古英语「全部为一」这个说法上，所以这个词量的是一个人离另一个声音有多远。

normal.en: Lonely comes from lone, and lone is alone with its first syllable clipped; alone literally said all one.
normal.cn: lonely 来自 lone，而 lone 是去掉开头音节的 alone；alone 字面就是「全部为一」。

normal.en: Alone states a fact and lonely states a feeling, which is why a person can be alone for a week without feeling lonely.
normal.cn: alone 说的是事实，lonely 说的是感受，所以一个人可以独处一周却不觉得寂寞。

normal.en: Add -ly to lone and you get lonely, the same suffix that builds friendly and lovely from nouns.
normal.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 就是 lonely，friendly 和 lovely 也是用同一个后缀从名词变来的。

normal.en: Loneliness adds -ness to lonely, turning a passing mood into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: loneliness 在 lonely 后加 -ness，把一时的情绪变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Lonesome is the American cousin; -some carries the sense of full of, so it is full of being alone.
normal.cn: lonesome 是美式英语的近亲；-some 带有「充满」的意味，所以它指「满是独处的感觉」。

abstract.en: All one is a picture before it is a phrase: a person pulling the whole world in until only himself is left.
abstract.cn: 「全部为一」先是一个画面，然后才是一个说法：一个人把整个世界收拢，直到只剩下自己。

abstract.en: A road and a tree can be lonely too, which shows English is willing to lend a human situation to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一条路、一棵树也能用 lonely，说明英语愿意把人的处境借给风景。

abstract.en: When the lights, the heating and the street noise are all present and the person is still lonely, the word is counting echoes rather than neighbours.
abstract.cn: 灯、暖气和街上的喧闹都在，人却仍然 lonely，说明这个词数的是回应，而不是身边的人。

examples.en: She felt lonely on her first night in the city.
examples.cn: 她在这个城市的第一夜感到孤独。

examples.en: They walked along a lonely road for hours.
examples.cn: 他们在一条荒凉的路上走了几个小时。

examples.en: A lonely tree stood in the middle of the field.
examples.cn: 田野中央立着一棵孤零零的树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「冷离」——冷冷地离开人群，身边空了，心里也就 lonely。

root: lone 是 alone 的截短形式；alone 由古英语 ān（一）加上 al-（全）构成，字面是「全部为一」，再加 -ly 便成 lonely。词根 ān 与拉丁语 ūnus（一）同出印欧语系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the state of being only one; it spreads from a person's sadness, to a place with no visitors, to an object with no neighbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只剩一个」的状态；它从人的难受，扩到无人经过的地方，再扩到旁边没有同类的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure under a street lamp, with a long shadow and no second pair of footsteps.
core.cn: 核心意象：路灯下只有一个人影，影子拉得很长，没有第二串脚步声。

branches.en: a lit window with only one chair at the table
branches.cn: 亮着的窗里只有一把椅子

branches.en: a phone that nobody calls on a birthday
branches.cn: 生日那天没有响过的电话

branches.en: an empty coast road at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时空荡的海边公路

branches.en: a village no bus stops at any more
branches.cn: 已经不再有班车停靠的村子

branches.en: one tree on a bare hilltop
branches.cn: 光秃山顶上的一棵树

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English numeral, the phrase that became alone, and two suffixes that turn a state into a feeling and a lasting condition.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的数词、演变成 alone 的短语，以及两个把状态变成感受和持续状况的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin unus and unicus belong to the same Indo-European family as the English word for one, which stands behind alone and lonely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus（一）与 unicus（唯一的）和英语中表示「一」的词同属一个印欧语系词族，而 alone、lonely 正是建立在「一」上。

definition_zh: 化学的；化学制品；化学品
definition_en: connected with chemistry; a substance used in or made by chemistry
core_image: 试管里起泡的液体，标签上写着复杂的名字
scene: 科学实验室的架子上，整齐排列着贴有标签的试剂瓶。 The teacher showed us a chemical that turns blue in water.
sceneCN: 这里 chemical 是「化学制品」（第 1 个义项：用于化学的物质）；句意为老师展示了遇水变蓝的化学试剂。

derivatives.zh: 由 chemical 加 -ly 构成，义为「以化学方式；用化学药剂」
由 chemistry 变形加 -ist 构成，义为「化学家；药剂师」

senses.title: A substance used in chemistry
senses.definition: a substance made or used in chemical processes, often with a special name
senses.definitionCN: 在化学过程中制造或使用的物质，常有专门名称
senses.example: The teacher showed us a chemical that turns blue in water.
senses.exampleCN: 老师展示了遇水变蓝的化学试剂。
senses.why: The science name becomes the name of the things the science works on.
senses.whyCN: 学科之名转为该学科所研究的物质之名。

senses.title: Connected with the science of substances
senses.definition: relating to chemistry or the substances it studies
senses.definitionCN: 与化学或其研究对象相关
senses.example: A chemical reaction made the liquid bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 化学反应让液体冒起了泡。
senses.why: The science adjective describes any change or property the science explains.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的形容词描述该学科所解释的一切变化与性质。

senses.title: Made by chemical processes, not natural
senses.definition: made using chemistry rather than by nature
senses.definitionCN: 借助化学方法制造，而非天然形成
senses.example: The farm uses fewer chemical fertilizers now.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场如今少用化学肥料。
senses.why: What the science makes stands against what nature makes, creating the man-made sense.
senses.whyCN: 科学造物与自然造物相对，于是产生「人工合成」之义。

intro.en: Chemical is built on chemistry, whose own story starts in the old craft of alchemy.
intro.cn: chemical 建立在 chemistry 之上，而后者的历史可追溯到古老的炼金术。

items.en: The root of alchemy is uncertain: Egyptian keme (black earth), Greek chuma (pouring) and Arabic al-kimiya are all proposed sources.
items.cn: alchemy 的词根存疑：埃及语 keme（黑土）、希腊语 chuma（浇注）与阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 均为候选来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin alchemia meant alchemy, the craft of changing matter.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 指炼金术，即转变物质的技艺。

items.en: French chimie separated the science of substances from the old magic craft.
items.cn: 法语 chimie 把物质之学与古老的秘术区分开来。

items.en: English chemistry, then chemical, named the science and its materials.
items.cn: 英语依次出现 chemistry 与 chemical，命名这门学科及其材料。

items.en: The adjective chemical settled for scientific change, and chemicals for the substances.
items.cn: 形容词 chemical 定型于科学变化，chemicals 指各类化学物质。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects science and substance words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收科学与物质类词。

entries.definition: The science of substances.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「化学」，是 chemical 的基础词。

entries.definition: A place where doctors treat patients.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诊所」，拼写与 chemical 词首相近。

entries.definition: By chemical means.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以化学方式」，由 chemical 派生。

entries.definition: A particular kind of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，与 chemical 的物质义相近。

entries.definition: A substance used in chemical tests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「试剂」，是实验室里的化学制品。

entries.definition: Connected with physics; not chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「物理的」，常与 chemical 并提对照。

normalIntro.en: Remember chemical by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chemical。

normal.en: chemical is chemistry plus -al.
normal.cn: chemical 是 chemistry 加 -al。

normal.en: a chemical reaction is what the science studies.
normal.cn: chemical reaction（化学反应）是这门学科研究的对象。

normal.en: chemist means both chemist and, in British English, pharmacist.
normal.cn: chemist 既指化学家，在英式英语里也指药剂师。

normal.en: alchemist is the older word, a seeker of gold.
normal.cn: alchemist（炼金术士）是更古老的词，指寻找黄金之人。

normal.en: farm chemicals help crops grow but must be used with care.
normal.cn: 农用化学品帮助庄稼生长，但须谨慎使用。

abstract.en: Picture coloured liquids bubbling quietly in test tubes.
abstract.cn: 想象试管里彩色液体静静冒泡。

abstract.en: Hear the small pop when two drops meet.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见两滴液体相遇时轻微的爆裂声。

abstract.en: Feel the cool glass of a labelled bottle in your hand.
abstract.cn: 感受贴着标签的试剂瓶冰凉的玻璃瓶身。

examples.en: The teacher showed us a chemical that turns blue in water.
examples.cn: 老师展示了遇水变蓝的化学试剂。

examples.en: A chemical reaction made the liquid bubble.
examples.cn: 化学反应让液体冒起了泡。

examples.en: The farm uses fewer chemical fertilizers now.
examples.cn: 这家农场如今少用化学肥料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开美口」——打开美妙的瓶口，倒出的是化学试剂。

root: 存疑源头（埃及语 keme 或希腊语 chuma）→ 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia（炼金术）→ 法语 chimie → 英语 chemistry → chemical；同族词有 chemist（化学家）、alchemist（炼金术士）。

sensesIntro.en: Chemical spreads from the science adjective to the substances and man-made products.
sensesIntro.cn: chemical 由学科形容词延伸到化学物质与人工合成品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: substances that chemistry studies and makes
core.cn: 核心意象：化学所研究与制造的物质

branches.en: A named substance
branches.cn: 有专名的物质

branches.en: Of the science
branches.cn: 属于化学这门学科

branches.en: Made by chemistry
branches.cn: 化学合成的

branches.cn: 实验室的试剂与溶液

branches.cn: 化肥与清洁剂

intro.cn: chemical 是学科名 chemistry 加形容词尾 -al 的形态。

latinIntro.cn: 更深的词根 alchemia 是中世纪拉丁语的「炼金术」。

an old seeker who tried to turn metal into gold

生化检测帮助医生诊断。

definition_zh: 讨论；商量；论述
definition_en: to talk about something with others to share ideas or decide
core_image: 几个人围着一张桌子交换意见
scene: 班会课上商量元旦晚会节目。 We will discuss the plan at the class meeting this afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 discuss 是「讨论」（第 1 个义项：交换看法）；句意是我们将在今天下午的班会上讨论这个计划。

derivatives.zh: discuss 加名词后缀构成，义为「讨论；商讨」
近义词，义为「争论」，含辩论语气

senses.title: To talk something over
senses.definition: to talk with others about a plan, problem or idea
senses.definitionCN: 与别人一起谈计划、问题或想法
senses.example: The family discussed where to spend the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人商量去哪里度假。
senses.why: The Latin discutere meant to shake apart; a discussion shakes a problem into pieces so everyone can look at it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 discutere 本义是「震散」；讨论把问题震成碎片，让大家都能看清。

senses.title: To write or speak about in detail
senses.definition: to examine a topic in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在讲话或文章里深入分析某个话题
senses.example: The book discusses the history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书论述了这座城市的历史。
senses.why: A careful writer also shakes apart a topic piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 认真的作者同样把话题逐层拆开来讲。

intro.en: Discuss comes from discutere, to shake apart.
intro.cn: discuss 出自 discutere，本义「震散」。

items.en: Latin discutere meant to shake apart or scatter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 discutere 意为震散、打散。

items.en: Quatere, the root inside, meant to shake.
items.cn: 词根 quatere 意为震动。

items.en: French discuter carried the sense of debating.
items.cn: 法语 discuter 带有辩论的意思。

items.en: English took discuss from Latin in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从拉丁语借入 discuss。

items.en: The shaking sense faded, leaving talking things over.
items.cn: 「震散」义逐渐消失，只留下讨论义。

note.en: These words share the quatere root or the talk-over field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 quatere 词根，或属于商量义场。

normal.cn: discuss it with your parents 是实用句型。

abstract.en: Picture friends leaning over one table.

definition_en: used to admit a fact and still state a contrasting point

senses.title: Admitting a fact before a contrast
senses.definition: used to admit one fact and then state another that contrasts with it
senses.definitionCN: 先承认一个事实，再说出与之相对的另一事实
senses.example: Although it rained, we went out.
senses.exampleCN: 虽然下雨，我们还是出去了。
senses.why: All plus though first meant even so, and the word opens by granting a fact that the main clause will oppose.
senses.whyCN: all 加 though 本意是「即便如此」，这个词先承认一个事实，主句再与之相对。

senses.title: Granting a quality in a short phrase
senses.definition: used before an adjective or a phrase to grant it
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词或短语前，表示承认这一点
senses.example: Although small, the room is warm.
senses.exampleCN: 房间虽小，却很暖和。
senses.why: The granted fact can shrink from a clause to a single quality, which gives the shorter sense of despite.
senses.whyCN: 被承认的事实可以从整句缩成一个性质，于是有较短的「尽管」用法。

sceneCN: 这里 some 是「一些」（第 1 个义项）；句意：桌上还有一些饼干。

senses.title: An unnamed amount
senses.definition: an amount or number that is not stated exactly
senses.definitionCN: 没有确切说明的数量
senses.example: There are some biscuits on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上还有一些饼干。
senses.why: Some marks a part of a whole without naming the size.
senses.whyCN: some 标出整体中的一部分，却不说大小。

senses.title: A certain one
senses.definition: used for a person or thing not exactly named
senses.definitionCN: 用于没有确切说出的人或事物
senses.example: Some man called while you were out.
senses.exampleCN: 你出去时有个男人打来电话。
senses.why: The same word covers an unnamed part and an unnamed member.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既能指未说明的部分，也能指未说明的成员。

senses.title: About, a little
senses.definition: used before numbers to mean about, or before adjectives to mean a little
senses.definitionCN: 用于数字前表示大约，或用于形容词前表示有点
senses.example: Some twenty people came to the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 大约二十个人来听了讲座。
senses.why: An unstated amount becomes an approximate amount.
senses.whyCN: 未说明的数量变成了近似的数量。

intro.en: Some is an old English word for an unspecified part.
intro.cn: some 是英语中表示未指明部分的古老词汇。

items.en: Sum meant some or a certain one.
items.cn: sum 意为一些或某一个。

items.en: The form settled as some.
items.cn: 词形固定为 some。

items.en: It kept the sense of an unstated amount.
items.cn: 它保留了未说明数量的含义。

items.en: It also came to mean a remarkable person or thing.
items.cn: 它也开始指了不起的人或事物。

items.en: It formed compounds such as something and somewhere.
items.cn: 它构成了 something、somewhere 等复合词。

note.en: Some is compared with look-alike words and words for unspecified amounts.
note.cn: 把 some 与形近词以及表示不确定数量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Some points at a part or a member without giving a number.
normalIntro.cn: some 指向一部分或某一个，却不给出数字。

normal.en: There are some biscuits on the table.
normal.cn: 桌上还有一些饼干。

normal.en: Some man called while you were out.
normal.cn: 你出去时有个男人打来电话。

normal.en: Some twenty people came to the talk.
normal.cn: 大约二十个人来听了讲座。

normal.en: Would you like some more tea?
normal.cn: 你想再来点茶吗？

normal.en: Some of the students arrived early.
normal.cn: 一些学生来得早。

abstract.en: Some is the word for what we know without counting.
abstract.cn: some 是用来表达「知道有，却没数过」的词。

abstract.en: An unnamed part is still a real part.
abstract.cn: 没有名字的部分，仍然是真实的部分。

abstract.en: Approximation is how language handles the unmeasured.
abstract.cn: 近似，是语言处理无法测量之事的方式。

examples.en: There are some biscuits on the table.
examples.cn: 桌上还有一些饼干。

examples.cn: 你出去时有个男人打来电话。

examples.en: Some of the students arrived early.
examples.cn: 一些学生来得早。

dict_mnemonic.text: some 表示「一些、某个」：some of 是「其中的一些」，some day 是「将来某一天」，some twenty 是「大约二十」；它还是 something、someone、somewhere 的开头。

root: 源自古英语 sum（一些、某一个），核心义「整体中未说明的一部分或成员」。

sensesIntro.en: Some means an unstated amount, a certain unnamed one, or about.
sensesIntro.cn: some 意为未说明的数量、某个未指名的人或物，或大约。

core.en: A part of something, left uncounted.
core.cn: 某物的一部分，不加计数。

branches.en: A few biscuits sit on a plate.
branches.cn: 盘子里放着几块饼干。

branches.en: A voice on the phone belongs to no known name.
branches.cn: 电话里的声音属于一个不知道名字的人。

branches.en: A crowd is counted roughly at a glance.
branches.cn: 一眼扫过去，人群被粗略计数。

branches.en: An unstated amount often becomes an approximate one.
branches.cn: 未说明的数量常常变成近似的数量。

branches.en: An unnamed member is a part of a larger group.
branches.cn: 未指名的成员是更大群体的一部分。

intro.en: Some builds a large family of compounds for unknown things and places.
intro.cn: some 构成一大族表示未知事物和地点的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Some has no Latin root; it comes from Old English sum.
latinIntro.cn: some 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 sum。

definition_zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；恼火的；狂热的；痴迷的；愚蠢的
definition_en: suffering from a serious mental illness, extremely angry in everyday speech, wildly enthusiastic, or foolish beyond reason
core_image: 一个人对着空椅子认真争辩，眼里的世界与旁人看到的完全不同
scene: 夜里的急诊走廊上，一位老人对着空气大声争辩，护士轻声请来值班医生。 The old man had gone mad and kept arguing with people who were not there.
sceneCN: 这里 mad 是「精神失常的、发疯的」（第 1 个义项：神志不清）；句意为老人已经疯了，一直跟并不存在的人争论。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊的灯、护士站、病历夹。

pos.zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；狂热的；愚蠢的

collocations.zh: 彻底疯了；疯得不可理喻

derivatives.zh: 由 mad 加 -ness 构成，义为「疯狂；精神失常」
由 mad 加 -ly 构成，义为「疯狂地；非正式口语中作『极其』」
由 mad 与 man 复合，义为「疯子；失去理智的男人」

senses.title: Mentally ill and out of touch with reality
senses.definition: suffering from a serious mental illness, so that the person cannot think or behave as others do
senses.definitionCN: 患有严重精神疾病，思考和举止与常人不同
senses.example: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。
senses.why: Old English gemǣd described a mind that had been altered out of its proper state, so illness of the mind is the oldest recorded sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemǣd 描述的是神志被改变、脱离正常状态，所以「心智患病」是这个词最早的记录义项。

senses.title: Very angry
senses.definition: extremely annoyed about something, in everyday informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中因某事而极为恼火
senses.example: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。
senses.why: Anger was pictured as a passing disturbance of the mind, and the word for a disordered mind slid into the word for a hot temper.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被想象成心智一时的失序，于是那个表示「头脑不正常」的词便滑向了「火气上来」这层意思。

senses.title: Wildly enthusiastic
senses.definition: so enthusiastic about someone or something that ordinary caution disappears
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物极为热衷，连平常的谨慎都没有了
senses.example: He is mad about vintage motorcycles and spends every weekend in the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他痴迷老式摩托车，每个周末都泡在车库里。
senses.why: Enthusiasm that sweeps away caution looks like the same loss of control, so the word moved from illness and anger to passion.
senses.whyCN: 那种把谨慎一扫而空的热情，看上去是同一种失控，于是这个词从疾病、愤怒又走到了迷恋。

senses.title: Foolish and ill judged
senses.definition: wildly foolish, used of plans or actions that no sensible person would attempt
senses.definitionCN: 极其愚蠢的，用于形容任何明白人都不会尝试的计划或举动
senses.example: Crossing the river in that storm was a mad thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样一场暴风雨里过河，是件极其愚蠢的事。
senses.why: Before it named illness, the word already meant foolish, so poor judgement remains the quiet base under every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 在指疾病之前，这个词早已表示「愚蠢」，所以「判断力差」一直是后来各义项底下沉默的底色。

intro.en: Mad is an Old English word for a disordered mind; its later senses of anger and passion grew from that base, and its deeper root is debated.
intro.cn: mad 是古英语中表示「神志失常」的词；后来「愤怒」与「痴迷」的意思都从这个底子长出来，更早的语源仍有争论。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic adjective, usually taken to mean changed or altered, and often explained as a mind shifted out of its normal state; the exact formation is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为意为「被改变的」，常被解释为神志偏出了正常状态；确切构成仍不确定。

items.en: Gemǣd is recorded in Old English for foolish and insane, and the ge- prefix gathers the word into a completed state.
items.cn: gemǣd 在古英语中记录为愚蠢的、精神失常的，前缀 ge- 把词收进一种已完成的状态。

items.en: Middle English drops the prefix and keeps mad, and by the fourteenth century the word also means angrily excited.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉前缀，保留 mad；到十四世纪，这个词也指「怒气冲冲的」。

items.en: The phrases mad about and mad for come to mean passionately fond, first of people and then of pursuits.
items.cn: 短语 mad about 与 mad for 开始表示「极其喜爱」，先用于人，后用于嗜好。

items.en: Modern English keeps the medical sense, uses mad for anger chiefly in informal American speech, and builds compounds such as mad cow and mad rush.
items.cn: 现代英语保留医学义项，「生气」义主要用于非正式美式口语，并造出疯牛病、疯狂冲刺一类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives, a compound and one word that merely shares the spelling; the near group gathers words for a disturbed mind and for anger.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词、一个复合词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示心智失常与愤怒的词。

entries.definition: The state of being insane, or wildly foolish behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常的状态；疯狂的行为；由 mad 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: In a wild or frantic way, and informally very much.
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂地；非正式口语中作「极其」；由 mad 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A man who is insane or acts with reckless violence.
entries.definitionCN: 疯子；行为狂暴失去理智的男人；由 mad 与 man 复合。

entries.definition: A polite form of address to a woman; only the spelling is close, the origin is French and unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的礼貌称呼；与 mad 只是拼写相近，词源来自法语，二者无关。

entries.definition: Wildly unreasonable or insane, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指极不理智或精神失常的。

entries.definition: Seriously mentally ill, or utterly foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 患严重精神病的；也指极其荒唐的。

entries.definition: Extremely angry.
Feeling strong displeasure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而感到强烈不快的。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English name for a mind out of order, and its family keeps returning to illness, temper and the passions that overrule caution.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语给「失序的心智」起的名字，它的同族词反复回到疾病、脾气，以及压过谨慎的激情。

normal.en: Old English already had gemǣd for foolish and insane, and modern mad is that word with its prefix worn away.
normal.cn: 古英语已有 gemǣd 表示愚蠢与精神失常，现代 mad 就是磨掉了前缀的那个词。

normal.en: The Old English prefix ge- often marks a completed state, so gemǣd pictured a mind that had been changed into something else.
normal.cn: 古英语前缀 ge- 常标记一种已完成的状态，所以 gemǣd 画出的是被改换成了别样东西的心智。

normal.en: Three ordinary endings carry the family: -ness makes madness, -ly makes madly, and man makes madman.
normal.cn: 三个常规词尾撑起这个词族：-ness 造出 madness，-ly 造出 madly，man 与 mad 合成 madman。

normal.en: Mad for anger is normal in American speech, while British speakers generally say angry instead.
normal.cn: 用 mad 表示生气在美式口语里很自然，英国人一般还是说 angry。

normal.en: To be mad about a hobby means far more than liking it: the hobby has taken over the weekends.
normal.cn: 对一项嗜好 mad about，远不只是「喜欢」：那项嗜好已经占满了周末。

abstract.en: A mind knocked out of place, like a clock whose hands have been bent by a blow.
abstract.cn: 一颗被撞离原位的心，就像一只被一击打歪了指针的钟。

abstract.en: Illness, anger and passion share one word because all three are states that take over the will.
abstract.cn: 疾病、愤怒与激情共用一个词，因为这三者都是接管了意志的状态。

abstract.en: Mad is what English says when reason has let go of the steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 当理智松开方向盘时，英语就说 mad。

examples.en: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
examples.cn: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。

examples.en: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
examples.cn: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。

examples.en: Many drivers go mad in the city's evening traffic.
examples.cn: 许多司机在城市的晚高峰里被逼得发疯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦德」——麦德脾气火爆，一点小事就跳起来发疯；记住 mad 是发疯、生气。

root: 古英语 gemǣd（愚蠢的、精神失常的），一般认为来自原始日耳曼语一个意为「被改变的」重构形式，确切构成存疑；中古英语磨去前缀 ge-，写作 mad。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mind out of its proper state; the senses then divide into mental illness, passing anger, burning enthusiasm and plain foolishness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是偏离正常状态的心智；义项由此分成精神疾病、一时的怒气、炽热的迷恋，以及单纯的愚蠢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man arguing earnestly with an empty chair, seeing a world no one else can see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人对着空椅子认真争辩，看见别人看不见的世界。

branches.en: a doctor watching a patient argue with an empty chair
branches.cn: 医生看着病人对空椅子争论

branches.en: a slammed door and a voice rising in the hall
branches.cn: 门被摔上，走廊里的嗓门高起来

branches.en: a man who cannot stop talking about his new motorbike
branches.cn: 一个人停不下来说他的新车

branches.en: a garage floor covered in half-repaired engines
branches.cn: 车库里满地是修了一半的发动机

branches.en: a boat pushed out into a black storm
branches.cn: 一条小船被推进漆黑的暴风雨

intro.en: An Old English adjective for a disordered mind, a Germanic prefix that has since worn away, and three English endings carry the word from illness to temper and passion.
intro.cn: 一个表示心智失序的古英语形容词、一个后来磨掉不存的日耳曼前缀，再加三个英语词尾，把这个词从疾病带到脾气与激情。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin insanus means insane, but it is built on a different root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 insanus 意为「精神失常的」，但它建立在另一个词根上。

definition_zh: 小说；虚构的事；编造的话
definition_en: a story made up from imagination, or something invented rather than true
core_image: 被写出来却不存在的世界：纸上的故事没有发生，却让人相信
scene: 书店角落的小说区亮着暖灯，孩子挑了一本冒险故事。 She picked a science fiction novel from the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 fiction 是「小说」（第 1 个义项：想象出来的故事作品）；句意为她从书架上挑了一本科幻小说。

pos.zh: 名词：虚构之事；编造的谎言

derivatives.zh: 由 fiction 加形容词后缀构成，义为「虚构的、小说式的」
来自同根拉丁形容词，义为「假想的、编造出来的」
加施动者后缀，指虚构写作者，较少用

senses.title: Novels and made-up stories
senses.definition: books and stories about imaginary people and events
senses.definitionCN: 关于想象中人物与事件的书和故事
senses.example: She reads fiction every night before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚睡前都读小说。
senses.why: The core image is a world written into existence, so the first sense is the written imagined story.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「被写出来的世界」，所以第一个义项就是成文的想象故事。

senses.title: Something invented and untrue
senses.definition: a claim or account that has been invented and is not true
senses.definitionCN: 被编造出来、并非真实的说法或叙述
senses.example: The report was pure fiction from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告从头到尾纯属虚构。
senses.why: The same imagined world leaves the page and pretends to be fact.
senses.whyCN: 同样的想象世界离开了书页，假装成事实，于是有了谎义。

senses.title: The act or category of inventing stories
senses.definition: the activity or genre of creating imagined stories as opposed to fact
senses.definitionCN: 与事实相对的、创作想象故事的门类或行为
senses.example: Fact and fiction overlap in his novels.
senses.exampleCN: 在他的小说里，事实与虚构相互交叠。
senses.why: Fiction names the whole territory where invention is allowed.
senses.whyCN: fiction 为「允许编造」的整个疆域命名，成为体裁概念。

intro.en: Fiction comes from a Latin verb about shaping and molding.
intro.cn: fiction 源自一个表示塑造、捏制的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Latin fingere meant to shape or mold, and fictio meant a shaping or feigning.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fingere 意为塑造，fictio 指一次塑造或假装。

items.en: Old French carried ficcion into Europe with the sense of invented account.
items.cn: 古法语以 ficcion 的形式传入欧洲，带有编造叙述的含义。

items.en: Middle English ficcioun first meant a false statement or pretense.
items.cn: 中古英语 ficcioun 先指虚假陈述或借口。

items.en: The modern sense of imagined literature became central over time.
items.cn: 现代英语中想象性文学的义项逐渐成为中心。

items.en: The modern language keeps the word in daily use.
items.cn: 现代英语仍在日常使用该词。

note.en: Fiction sits next to novel and legend but they are not the same size of word.
note.cn: fiction 与 novel、legend 相邻，但词的范围大小不同。

entries.definition: adjective meaning invented, not real
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：虚构的、非真实的

entries.definition: adjective from the same Latin root, meaning made up
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词：编造的、假想的

entries.definition: rubbing force between surfaces; only one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦（力）；与 fiction 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: a long written fictional story in book form
entries.definitionCN: 长篇虚构故事书，是 fiction 的一种具体形式

entries.definition: an old story that may mix history and imagination
entries.definitionCN: 古老传说，介于史实与想象之间

entries.definition: highly imaginative fiction about impossible worlds
entries.definitionCN: 奇幻作品，想象力更放开的 fiction 分支

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to fix fiction in your memory.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子把 fiction 钉进记忆。

normal.en: Fiction shares its root with figure: a shaped form rather than a real person.
normal.cn: fiction 与 figure 同根：是被塑造的形象，而非真人。

normal.en: Science fiction is the most famous member of the family.
normal.cn: science fiction 是这个家族最有名的成员。

normal.en: A lie is fiction pretending to be news.
normal.cn: 谎言是假装成新闻的 fiction。

normal.en: Fiction ends in -tion like creation: both make something from nothing.
normal.cn: fiction 以 -tion 结尾，与 creation 一样：都从无到有。

normal.en: Bookshop signs use Fiction over the shelves of invented stories.
normal.cn: 书店的 Fiction 标牌下面摆的全是虚构故事。

abstract.en: Fiction is a door in the page: step in and the world exists.
abstract.cn: fiction 是书页里的一扇门：踏进去，世界就存在。

abstract.en: Picture ink shaping itself into people who never lived.
abstract.cn: 想象墨水把自己捏成从未活过的人。

abstract.en: Between fact and dream there is a workshop; its name is fiction.
abstract.cn: 在事实与梦之间有一间工坊，它的名字叫 fiction。

examples.en: Journey to the West blends fact and fiction.
examples.cn: 《西游记》混合了事实与虚构。

examples.en: The rumor turned out to be complete fiction.
examples.cn: 那谣言原来是彻头彻尾的编造。

examples.en: He won a prize for his first work of fiction.

senses.why: Dug from the dark earth and burned in the dark stove, the black stone keeps houses warm.

intro.en: Coal is an old fire word: people have named it since they first fed stoves.

items.en: The Germanic base *kulo meant something burned or charred.
items.cn: 日耳曼词基 *kulo 指被烧过或烧焦之物。

items.en: Old English col first meant charcoal, the burnt wood.
items.cn: 古英语 col 最初指木炭，即烧过的木头。

items.en: When mined stone fuel spread, Middle English gave the name to mineral coal.
items.cn: 当开采的石头燃料普及，中古英语把这名字给了矿物煤。

items.en: Modern English coal means the mined fuel; the wood fuel became charcoal.
items.cn: 现代英语 coal 指开采的煤；木头燃料改称 charcoal。

items.en: Industrial English added coalfield, coal mine and coal fire.
items.cn: 工业时代的英语又添了 coalfield、coal mine、coal fire 等词。

note.en: The first group collects the coal family; the second collects fuel words.
note.cn: 第一组收 coal 词族，第二组收燃料类词。

senses.title: Easy to press

senses.definitionCN: 容易按压、弯曲或塑形，不坚硬的
senses.example: The baby's skin is soft.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的皮肤很柔软。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of texture.

senses.title: Gentle

senses.definitionCN: 温和而不粗鲁、不强硬的

senses.title: Following a line

senses.title: Together with

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: andlang meant the full length: along is movement beside a long line.

normal.en: The same family also gives alongside and alongshore.

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase along the road.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「沿着道路」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of along in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 along 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: following the length of something, or forward, or together with someone.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「沿着」时用它。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of along grows from one core image: a path running beside a river far into the distance.
sensesIntro.cn: along 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：小路沿河岸一直伸向远处。

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：向前。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：顺着某物的长度、向前。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: Together with.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：一起；随同。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖意义的边缘：顺着某物的长度、一起；随同。

definition_zh: 井；水井；油井；（用作感叹或停顿）嗯、那么；很好地
definition_en: a deep hole dug or drilled into the ground to reach water, oil or gas, and also the old adverb of good, kept in idioms
core_image: 村口一块圆石井栏，辘轳上垂下一只木桶，井口冒着凉气
scene: 天刚亮，妇人摇着辘轳把木桶从井里提上来，水面上还浮着一层白雾。 Every morning she draws a bucket of water from the old well behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 well 是「水井」（第 1 个义项：为取水而向地下挖的深洞）；句意为她每天早上都从屋后那口老井里打上一桶水。石井栏、辘轳、冒凉气的井口就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A hole dug for water
senses.definition: a deep hole in the ground, usually lined with stone or brick, from which water is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 在地上挖出的深洞，常用石块或砖砌壁，供人从中取水
senses.example: Every morning she draws a bucket of water from the old well behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上都从屋后那口老井里打一桶水。
senses.why: The oldest meaning of the word is simply this hole; in Old English wiell also covered a spring that bubbles up by itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思就是这个洞；古英语里的 wiell 同时也指自动涌出的泉水。

senses.title: A hole drilled for oil or gas
senses.definition: a deep bore made by machine in order to take oil, gas or water from far below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 用机械向地层深处钻出的孔道，用以获取石油、天然气或地下水
senses.example: The company shut down three wells when the price of oil fell.
senses.exampleCN: 油价下跌时，这家公司关掉了三口油井。
senses.why: Industry kept the shape of the old water hole and put it over any vertical shaft that taps a fluid underground.
senses.whyCN: 工业沿用了古老水井的形象，把任何伸向地下流体的竖直钻孔都叫作井。

senses.title: A source that keeps giving
senses.definition: in figurative use, a place or thing from which something seems to flow endlessly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某种东西仿佛源源不断流出的来源
senses.example: Her letters are a well of stories about the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的来信是老城故事的源泉。
senses.why: A well never empties when you keep drawing from it, so the word became a picture of inexhaustible supply.
senses.whyCN: 只要不断打水，井也不会干，于是这个词成了取之不尽的供应之图像。

senses.title: In a good way
senses.definition: the adverb form of good, describing an action done in a skilful or pleasing manner
senses.definitionCN: good 的副词形式，说明某动作做得有技巧、令人满意
senses.example: She sings well for someone who has never had a lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个从没上过课的人来说，她唱得很好了。
senses.why: This is a different word in origin, the adverb of good, which simply fell into the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思来源不同，本是 good 的副词，只是拼写恰好合到了一起。

senses.title: In good health
senses.definition: used after a verb such as be or feel to say that someone is not ill
senses.definitionCN: 用在 be、feel 之后，表示某人身体没有病
senses.example: He was not well last week, so he stayed at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他上星期身体不舒服，所以待在家里。
senses.why: Health was once described as a state of being in good order, and the adverb simply filled that slot.
senses.whyCN: 健康过去被说成处于良好的状态，而这个副词正好占住了那个位置。

senses.title: A pause word at the start
senses.definition: spoken at the beginning of a remark to gain time or to soften what follows
senses.definitionCN: 说话开头使用，用来争取时间或让后面的话显得缓和
senses.example: Well, I am not sure that is the best plan.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，我不确定那是不是最好的方案。
senses.why: The same short syllable is a place-holder, much like the opening of a conversation that needs a moment before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短音节被当作占位的声音，就像一句需要停顿片刻才开口的话的开头。

intro.en: Well as a water hole goes back to Old English wiell, a spring or a bubbling up, and it has been spelled well since the Middle English period.
intro.cn: 表示水井的 well 可追溯到古英语 wiell（泉、涌出），自中古英语时期起拼作 well。

items.en: Wiell meant a spring that came up out of the ground, and the word was used for any source of water.
items.cn: wiell 指从地下涌出的泉水，这个词也用来指任何水源。

items.en: A second word, wel, was the adverb meaning in a good way, and it stood beside the noun without any link.
items.cn: 另一个词 wel 是表示「良好地」的副词，它与名词并列存在，彼此并无联系。

items.en: In Middle English the two forms came to the same spelling, and the noun began to mean a dug shaft as well as a spring.
items.cn: 在中古英语中两种形式拼写趋同，名词也从泉水的意思扩展到人工挖成的井。

items.en: Deeper drilling brought the sense of an oil well, and the water picture stayed as a metaphor for abundance.
items.cn: 更深的钻探带来了油井之义，而水的形象则作为丰足的比喻保留下来。

items.en: The old adverb survives in fixed phrases such as do well, get well and as well as.
items.cn: 古老的副词在 do well、get well、as well as 等固定短语中保存下来。

note.en: The first group gathers words that share the shape of a hole or its mouth, the second the words for a source and for being in good condition.
note.cn: 第一组收与洞口、井口形体相关的词，第二组收表示来源与良好状态的说法。

A large dug hollow, often for storing or trapping.
Water that rises by itself out of the ground.
The long straight passage of a well or a mine.
The place from which something comes, abstract as well as physical.
Free from illness, the adjective that matches being well.
In the right or expected way, as the adverb of doing something well.
A short opening word that softens the start of a remark, like a spoken well.

normalIntro.en: Two different words, a water hole and an old adverb, were written the same way, so the entry has to keep both pictures in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 一个水井名词和一个古老副词被写成了同一个形状，所以这个词条要同时记住两幅画面。

normal.en: See the w, mirrored as the walls of a round shaft, and the o, the mouth at the top.
normal.cn: 想字母 w 像圆井壁的两侧，字母 o 像井口。

normal.en: Water wells are dug; oil wells are drilled, but both are vertical tubes into the dark.
normal.cn: 水井是挖的，油井是钻的，但两者都是伸进黑暗里的竖管。

normal.en: A well of stories is the same picture with the water turned into words.
normal.cn: 「故事之井」是同一幅画面，只是水换成了语言。

normal.en: Well as an adverb hides in do well, get well and as well as.
normal.cn: 作副词的 well 藏在 do well、get well 和 as well as 里。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence it is only a soft noise that buys a second.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，它只是一个买来一秒钟的软声音。

abstract.en: Feel the cold air rising out of a stone mouth.
abstract.cn: 感受凉气从石头做的嘴里往上冒。

abstract.en: Hear a bucket rope creak and then stop.
abstract.cn: 听井绳吱呀作响，然后停住。

abstract.en: Picture a level of water that never moves though it is drawn from daily.
abstract.cn: 想一个天天被打水却始终不动的水面。

examples.en: The villagers still wash clothes beside the well.
examples.cn: 村民仍然在井边洗衣服。

examples.en: She did well in the exam without much preparation.
examples.cn: 她没怎么复习，考试却考得很好。

examples.en: Well, we can talk about it again tomorrow.
examples.cn: 嗯，我们明天可以再谈这件事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂哦」——站在井边往下喂一声，回声从井底慢慢升上来。

root: 古英语 wiell（泉、涌出）与副词 wel（良好地）在中古英语时期拼写成形，成为同一个 well；另有 adj. good 的副词比较级 better、best。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts at a hole that gives water, widens to any shaft into the ground, becomes a picture of endless supply, and finally covers the old adverb of good and its health sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从出水的洞开始，扩大到任何伸入地下的竖井，再成为取之不尽的比喻，最后还覆盖了 good 的副词及健康之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone mouth in the ground with a rope hanging into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面上一张石头的嘴，一根绳子垂进去。

branches.en: The village branch: a bucket lifted from cold water.
branches.cn: 村庄分支：从冷水里提起的木桶。

branches.en: The industrial branch: three oil wells shut down.
branches.cn: 工业分支：关停的三口油井。

branches.en: The figurative branch: letters as a well of stories.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：作为故事之井的来信。

branches.en: The adverb branch: singing well and the pause word well.
branches.cn: 副词分支：唱得好，以及开口时的「嗯」。

branches.en: The health branch: not well, so staying at home.
branches.cn: 健康分支：身体不好，于是待在家里。

intro.en: Well is a whole Old English word rather than a derived form, but it joins freely in compounds such as wellness and wellhead, and in set phrases with the old adverb.
intro.cn: well 是完整的古英语词而非派生词，但它能自由参与 wellness、wellhead 这类复合词，也与古老副词构成固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source behind it; the Latin entries below are only cognate forms of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼词，背后没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目只是同一词族的同源形式。

items.example: It is the plain noun we still use.
items.exampleCN: 这就是我们仍在使用的朴素名词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded shape.

items.example: The old adverb keeps an irregular comparative.

definition_zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划；投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）
definition_en: a planned piece of work, or to throw something forward in space, time, or imagination
core_image: 把一张纸向前抛出去，纸面在空中展开成一块可见的平面
scene: 会议室里，团队把目标、时间线、负责人写在墙上。 The whole project is pinned to the wall, with its goals, its timeline and the name of the person who owns each part.
sceneCN: 这里 project 是「项目、工程」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而规划的一整块工作）；句意：整个项目都贴在墙上，写着目标、时间线，以及每一部分的负责人。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、便利贴、时间线、负责人照片、马克笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）；使（影像）成像

senses.title: A planned piece of work
senses.definition: a planned undertaking with a goal, a timetable, and resources
senses.definitionCN: 有计划、有目标、有时间与资源的任务
senses.example: The bridge project will take five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的工程要五年。
senses.why: Latin proiectum is 'something thrown forward'. A project is a plan thrown ahead of you, a future state you have already sketched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proiectum 是“被抛向前之物”。project 是被投到你前方的计划，一幅你已勾画出的未来图景。

senses.title: A research or study topic
senses.definition: a specific piece of research or academic work
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体的研究或学术工作
senses.example: She is working on a project about urban birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做一个关于城市鸟类的课题。
senses.why: Schools and labs cut knowledge into manageable pieces. Each project is a bounded task with its own question, method, and deadline.
senses.whyCN: 学校与实验室把知识切成可处理的块。每个 project 都是有界任务，有自己的问题、方法与期限。

senses.title: To estimate or forecast
senses.definition: to calculate what a quantity will be in the future
senses.definitionCN: 计算某数量在未来会是多少
senses.example: Analysts project a rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计需求上升。
senses.why: Forecasting is throwing a number forward in time. The same verb that launches an object through space launches a figure into next year.
senses.whyCN: 预测是把一个数字抛向未来。同一个把物体抛过空间的动词，也把数字抛进明年。

senses.title: To throw forward physically
senses.definition: to throw or cast something forward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向前抛
senses.example: The machine projects balls at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器高速抛出球。
senses.why: This is the literal core: iacere 'to throw' with pro- 'forward'. Every abstract sense is a metaphor built on this physical cast.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：iacere“投”加 pro-“向前”。一切抽象义都建在这个物理抛掷上。

senses.title: To cast an image onto a surface
senses.definition: to cause light or an image to fall on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使光或影像落在某个表面
senses.example: The device projects the map onto the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 设备把地图投射到墙上。
senses.why: Light is thrown forward and lands on a screen. The projector is the object that throws, and the image is what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 光被抛向前方，落在屏幕上。projector 是抛掷之物，影像则是到达之物。

senses.title: To extend outward
senses.definition: of a part, to stick out beyond the main body
senses.definitionCN: 某部分超出主体向外伸
senses.example: The balcony projects over the street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台向街道上方凸出。
senses.why: A shape that juts out is literally thrown beyond the wall. Architecture uses the word for any part that advances past its base.
senses.whyCN: 向外突出的形状，字面上被抛出了墙外。建筑学用这个词指任何越过基线的部分。

senses.title: To convey an impression
senses.definition: to communicate a quality or image to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人传达某种品质或形象
senses.example: A good speaker projects confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 好的演讲者展现自信。
senses.why: Social presence is treated as a projection: an inner state is thrown outward so others can see it. The word implies deliberate display.
senses.whyCN: 社会在场被当作一种投射：内在状态被抛到外面，让他人看见。这个词隐含刻意的展示。

senses.title: To predict by extrapolation
senses.definition: to extend a trend or pattern into the future
senses.definitionCN: 把趋势或模式延伸到未来
senses.example: The model projects growth through 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 模型推算增长将持续到 2030 年。
senses.why: Statistics throws a line forward from known points. Projection is the noun, and it always carries the caveat that the future may not land where the line points.
senses.whyCN: 统计把一条线从已知点向前抛。projection 是名词，且总带着警告：未来未必落在线的落点。

senses.title: To protrude anatomically
senses.definition: of a body part, to stick out from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分从表面突出
senses.example: The jaw projects forward.
senses.exampleCN: 下颌向前突出。
senses.why: Bones and features can be thrown beyond the body's outline. Anatomy uses the same spatial verb as architecture, applied to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 骨与特征可以超出身体轮廓。解剖学把与建筑相同的空间动词用于肉体。

senses.title: To map onto a plane (geometry)
senses.definition: to represent a figure on a plane by drawing lines from it
senses.definitionCN: 用射线把图形表示到平面上
senses.example: Project the sphere onto a flat map.
senses.exampleCN: 把球面投影到平面地图上。
senses.why: Geometry formalizes the light image: points are carried along rays to a surface. Map projections keep the same metaphor, with distortion as the price.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把光的意象形式化：点沿射线被带到表面。地图投影保留同一隐喻，代价是变形。

intro.en: Project is a throwing word. Latin proicere joins pro- 'forward' to iacere 'to throw'. A plan, an image, a forecast, and a balcony are all things thrown ahead of the body.
intro.cn: project 是一个抛掷词。拉丁语 proicere 把 pro-“向前”与 iacere“投”结合。计划、影像、预测与阳台，都是被抛到身体前方的东西。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'a plan, scheme, design'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“计划、方案、设计”。

items.en: From Latin proiectum 'something thrown forth', neuter past participle of proicere 'throw forward' = pro- 'forward' + iacere 'to throw'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 proiectum“被抛向前之物”，是 proicere“向前抛”的中性过去分词 = pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”。

items.en: iacere also gives eject, inject, reject, subject, and object. The family is about throwing, and the prefix sets the direction.
items.cn: iacere 还生成 eject、inject、reject、subject、object。这个词族关乎投掷，前缀定方向。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense 'to throw or cast forward'.
items.cn: 动词出现，义为“向前投掷”。

items.en: Projection extends to optics, psychology (projecting an image), and statistics (projecting a trend).
items.cn: projection 扩展到光学、心理学（投射形象）与统计学（推算趋势）。

items.en: Modern English uses project for both a planned task and the act of throwing an image, a forecast, or a shape forward.
items.cn: 现代英语用 project 既指计划任务，也指把影像、预测或形状向前抛出的动作。

note.en: The first group shares the iacere root and the -ject shape; the second is about words that also mean a plan or a forecast.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iacere 词根与 -ject 形态，第二组看同样表示“计划”或“预测”的词。

entries.definition: the act of projecting; a forecast or a protruding part.
a device that throws an image onto a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把影像投到表面的设备。

entries.definition: to throw back; to refuse. It is re- 'back' + iacere.
entries.definitionCN: 掷回；拒绝。它是 re-“向后”+ iacere。

entries.definition: a detailed proposal for doing something. It emphasizes intention, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的详细提议。它强调意图，而非工作本身。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It matches project sense 3 but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将发生之事的陈述。它对应 project 第 3 义，但更具体。

entries.definition: a risky new business or activity. It stresses risk rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的新事业。它强调风险，而非规划。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin iacere 'throw', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the reject/inject/eject family, and the optics and statistics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 iacere“投”、前缀 pro-“向前”、reject/inject/eject 词族，以及光学与统计用法。

normal.en: Iacere means 'throw'; pro- means 'forward'. A project is something thrown ahead of you.
normal.cn: iacere 意为“投”；pro- 意为“向前”。project 是被抛到你前方的东西。

normal.en: Reject throws back, inject throws in, eject throws out, project throws forward: the prefix is the direction.
normal.cn: reject 掷回，inject 掷入，eject 掷出，project 掷向前：前缀就是方向。

normal.en: A projector throws light; a balcony throws itself beyond the wall; a forecast throws a number into next year.
normal.cn: 投影仪抛光；阳台把自己抛出墙外；预测把数字抛进明年。

normal.en: Project management is planning seen as a launched object: it has a target, a trajectory, and a landing date.
normal.cn: 项目管理就是把计划看作被发射的物体：它有目标、弹道与落地日期。

normal.en: Projecting confidence is throwing an inner state outward so others can catch it.
normal.cn: 展现自信，是把内在状态抛到外面，让他人接住。

abstract.en: Planning is projective: to make a project is to live in a future you have already thrown into view.
abstract.cn: 规划是投射性的：做一个项目，就是住在一个已被你抛入视野的未来里。

abstract.en: Every projection distorts: a map, a forecast, and a self-image all flatten something three-dimensional.
abstract.cn: 每一种投影都会变形：地图、预测与自我形象，都把某种立体之物压平。

abstract.en: The word ties action to imagination: what we throw forward is first an object of thought, then a thing in the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词把行动与想象绑在一起：我们抛向前方的，先是思想的对象，然后才是世界中的实物。

examples.en: The team finished the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队提前完成了项目。

examples.en: The film was projected onto a huge screen.
examples.cn: 影片被投射到一块巨大的屏幕上。

examples.en: Sales are projected to grow by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额预计增长百分之十。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若杰克特”——扑向前，像杰克特（飞镖）一样被抛出 → project 项目、投射

root: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”= pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”；过去分词 proiectum。同族有 eject、inject、reject、subject。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of project, all one throw. What is thrown can be a plan (a project), an image (a projection), a number (a forecast), a wall (a balcony), or a self (a persona).
sensesIntro.cn: project 的十个义项，都是同一次抛掷。被抛出的可以是计划（项目）、影像（投影）、数字（预测）、墙体（阳台），或自我（形象）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something thrown forward from the body into space or time.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从身体被抛向前方，进入空间或时间。

branches.en: PLAN: a future task sketched and thrown ahead.
branches.cn: 计划：被勾画并抛向前方的未来任务。

branches.en: CAST: physical throwing, light onto a surface, and geometric projection.
branches.cn: 投射：物理抛掷、光落表面与几何投影。

branches.en: PROTRUDE: a part thrown beyond the outline, in buildings and bodies.
branches.cn: 凸出：在建筑与身体中超出轮廓的部分。

branches.en: PERSONA: an inner state thrown outward for others to see.
branches.cn: 形象：内在状态被抛向外，供他人看见。

branches.en: FORECAST: a number or trend carried into the future.
branches.cn: 预测：被带到未来的数字或趋势。

intro.en: Project is noun and verb. English adds -ion, -or, and -ed, and the root iacere also builds reject, inject, eject, and subject.
intro.cn: project 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ed，词根 iacere 还构成 reject、inject、eject、subject。

latinIntro.en: Latin proicere 'throw forward' and its participle proiectum stand beside iacere 'throw'. The -ject family is a set of directions: re- back, in- in, e- out, pro- forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”及其分词 proiectum 旁边是 iacere“投”。-ject 词族是一组方向：re- 向后、in- 向内、e- 向外、pro- 向前。

items.meaningCN: 投射；预测；凸出（-ion 构成名词）

definition_zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子；拼合
definition_en: a part cut or broken from something larger; a single work of art or music; one of the objects moved in a board game; to join parts into a whole
core_image: 一块带釉的碎瓷片躺在桌上，断口处仍泛着光
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱落地，一只旧碗碎成几块，最大的那块还带着半圈蓝花。 She picked up the largest piece and turned it over in her hand.
sceneCN: 这里 piece 指「一块、一片」（第 1 个义项：从整体上分下来的一部分）；句意为她捡起最大的那一块，在手里翻看。图中可辨识物件：碎瓷片、蓝花、落地的纸箱。

pos.zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子

derivatives.zh: 由 piece 加古英语后缀 -meal（逐……地）构成，义为「一件一件的；零碎的」
由 a 与 piece 合成，义为「每人；各」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，义为「杰作」

senses.title: A part broken or cut from something larger
senses.definition: a part separated from a whole, especially one small enough to hold or to see as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 从整体上分离出来的一部分，尤指小到可以拿在手里或单独看见的一块
senses.example: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。
senses.why: Medieval Latin petia named a fragment, and English took the word with that broken-off shape already inside it, so the first sense is the shard rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 本指碎片，英语借来时，「从整体上断下来的一块」这个形状已经装在词里，所以最早的义项是碎片而非整体。

senses.title: A single work of art, music, or writing
senses.definition: one complete work, especially a short musical composition, a painting, or a short text
senses.definitionCN: 一件完整的作品，尤指短小的乐曲、一幅画或一段短文
senses.example: The band played a new piece at the end of the set.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在演出末尾演奏了一首新作品。
senses.why: A work is also a unit that can be counted and handed over, so the noun that counted fragments came to count finished works, each treated as one whole.
senses.whyCN: 作品同样是可以清点、可以交到别人手里的一个单位，于是原本数碎块的名词也用来数成品，每一件都被当作一个整体。

senses.title: One of the objects moved in a board game
senses.definition: one of the small objects that a player moves on a board, as in chess or draughts
senses.definitionCN: 棋手在棋盘上移动的小物件之一，如国际象棋或跳棋中的棋子
senses.example: He moved a single piece and the whole game turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。
senses.why: A game set is a collection of small separate units, and each one is literally a piece taken out of the box, which is why the word needed no stretching here.
senses.whyCN: 一副棋就是一小堆彼此分开的小单位，每一枚本来就是从盒子里取出来的一块，所以这个词在这里根本不必引申。

senses.title: To join parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put the separate parts of something together until they form a whole, often by patient work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分开的各个部分合在一起，直到形成整体，常需耐心
senses.example: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: what was broken into pieces is put back, and the word now watches the fragments travel toward a whole instead of away from it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向倒过来：被分成块的东西重新合起来，这个词现在看着碎块朝整体走，而不是从整体散开。

intro.en: Piece came through Old French from a medieval Latin word for a fragment, and that word's own earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: piece 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语中表示碎片的一个词，而那个词更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin petia or petium meant a piece or fragment, but its earlier origin is uncertain and a Gaulish source is often suggested.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium 意为一块、碎片，但它更早的来源不确定，常有人推测来自高卢语。

items.en: Old French piece named a part, a fragment, or a coin, and carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 piece 指一部分、碎片或一枚钱币，诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English piece could mean a fragment, a share, or a particular item, and the spelling settled without the French accent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 piece 可指碎片、份额或某一件事物，拼写逐渐定型，去掉了法语的变音记号。

items.en: By the sixteenth century a piece could be a work of art or music, because such a work is exactly one countable item.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，piece 已可指一件艺术品或一首乐曲，因为这样一件作品恰好就是一个可以清点的事项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fragment at the centre and builds phrasal verbs such as piece together, where the fragments are put back.
items.cn: 现代英语仍以碎片为中心，并造出 piece together 这类短语动词，让碎片重新拼回去。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same stem plus two words that only share the sound or the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for parts and fragments.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式，外加两个只在发音或拼写上相近的词；近义组收表示部分与碎片的词。

entries.definition: Done in separate stages or small amounts rather than all at once.
entries.definitionCN: 分成若干阶段或小份来做，而非一次完成。

entries.definition: For each person or thing; one to each.
A state of quiet and freedom from war; it sounds the same but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 没有战争与纷扰的安宁状态；发音相同，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To make a hole through something with a sharp point; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物在物体上穿出孔洞；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small part broken off from something.
entries.definitionCN: 从某物上断下的一小块。

entries.definition: A part of something larger, often a share given to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 较大事物的一部分，常指分给某人的份额。

entries.definition: A small piece or amount of something.
One of the parts into which something is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被分成的若干部分之一。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from a fragment, and its family keeps counting parts, works, and small movable units.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从碎片出发，它的词族一直在数部分、作品和可以移动的小单位。

normal.en: Piece came from Old French, and the medieval Latin form behind it already meant a fragment.
normal.cn: piece 来自古法语，而它背后的中世纪拉丁语形式本就已经指碎片。

normal.en: Piece together is the noun turned into a verb: the fragments are made to travel back into a whole.
normal.cn: piece together 是名词转成动词：碎块被赶回整体里去。

normal.en: Peace sounds exactly the same but comes from a different root, so the two must be kept apart in writing.
normal.cn: peace 读音完全相同，但来自另一个词根，所以写的时候必须把两者分开。

normal.en: Apiece adds a to piece and means one for each, as in tickets at ten pounds apiece.
normal.cn: apiece 在 piece 前加 a，意为「每人一个」，如门票每张十英镑。

normal.en: A piece of music and a piece of news both use piece as a counter for one item, not as a fragment.
normal.cn: 「一首乐曲」与「一则消息」里的 piece 都是清点事项的量词用法，而不是碎片。

abstract.en: The same word counts a broken shard, a finished sonata and a chessman, because English counts parts and wholes with one noun.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既数碎瓷片，也数写完的奏鸣曲和一枚棋子，因为英语用一个名词同时数部分与整体。

abstract.en: To piece something together is to trust that the fragments still carry the shape of what they came from.
abstract.cn: 把东西拼起来，就是相信这些碎片仍然带着它们原来所属之物的形状。

abstract.en: A piece is always smaller than its whole, except when the whole is a work of art, and then the piece is the whole.
abstract.cn: 一块总比它的整体小，除非那个整体是一件作品，这时「一件」就等于整体。

examples.en: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
examples.cn: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。

examples.en: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
examples.cn: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。

examples.en: He moved one piece and the game changed.
examples.cn: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈死」——碗被劈成几块，一块就是 a piece；记住 piece 是碎片、一块。

root: 古法语 piece 来自中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium（一块、碎片），更早来源不确定，常推测与高卢语有关；没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a part separated from a whole; from that one shard grow the countable work, the chessman, and the verb that puts fragments back together.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从整体上分下来的一块；由这一块碎片长出可清点的作品、棋盘上的棋子，以及把碎块拼回整体的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shard of glazed china lying on a table, its broken edge still shining.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块带釉的碎瓷片躺在桌上，断口处仍泛着光。

branches.en: a shard of blue-patterned china on the floor
branches.cn: 地上一块带蓝花的瓷片

branches.en: a short piano work printed on a single page
branches.cn: 印在一页纸上的短小钢琴曲

branches.en: a chessman lifted between two fingers
branches.cn: 两根手指夹起的一枚棋子

branches.en: a torn map spread out and matched edge to edge
branches.cn: 摊开的地图被一处处对上边

branches.en: a bowl repaired with visible seams
branches.cn: 用看得见的接缝补好的碗

latinIntro.cn: 记录中唯一的拉丁形式是中世纪拉丁语的 petia，它自身的来源并不确定，所以这一条列得简短而谨慎。

definition_zh: 队伍；排队；队列；（旧）辫子
definition_en: a line of people waiting for something; to wait in such a line; a list of items handled in the order they arrive, especially in computing; a long plait of hair
core_image: 雨里一条沿着墙根排开的长队，伞尖连成一线
scene: 剧院门外，雨点打在伞面上，人们把伞收低，一个接一个站在售票窗口前的长队里。 A long queue stretched along the wet pavement outside the theatre.
sceneCN: 这里 queue 是「排队等候的队伍」（第 1 个义项：一列等待的人）；句意为一条长队沿着剧院外湿漉漉的路面延伸开去。画面里可留意：伞面、湿路面、连成一线的人。

derivatives.zh: queue 加 -ing，指排队等候这件事或排队系统
queue 与 jumper 复合，指插队的人

senses.title: A line of people waiting
senses.definition: a line of people standing one behind another while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 人们一个接一个站着等待某物的行列
senses.example: A long queue formed outside the ticket office.
senses.exampleCN: 售票处外排起了长队。
senses.why: Old French cue meant a tail, and a line of waiting people was seen as a tail trailing from a counter.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 cue 意为尾巴，一列等待的人被看作从柜台后拖出来的一条尾巴。

senses.title: To wait in a line
senses.definition: to stand in a line and wait for your turn
senses.definitionCN: 站在队伍里等候轮到自己
senses.example: We queued for two hours in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们冒雨排了两个小时的队。
senses.why: Once the noun named the line, the verb naturally named the act of standing in it.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这条队伍，动词自然就指站在队伍里等候这一动作。

senses.title: A list handled in arrival order
senses.definition: a store of items in which the first one to arrive is the first one to be handled
senses.definitionCN: 一种存储结构，先到达的项先被处理
senses.example: The printer keeps every job in a queue until the paper is loaded.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机把每个任务都放进队列，直到装好纸才处理。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the image of people waiting in a line, because a queue serves first come, first served.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了人们排队等候的形象，因为队列正是先到先服务。

senses.title: A long plait of hair
senses.definition: a long braid of hair worn hanging down the back, as in older portraits
senses.definitionCN: 垂在背后的长发辫，见于旧时画像
senses.example: In the old portrait her hair hangs in a long queue.
senses.exampleCN: 在那幅旧画像里，她的头发梳成一条长辫垂在背后。
senses.why: The tail sense of the French word survived in English for a plait of hair, which really does hang like a tail.
senses.whyCN: 法语词中「尾巴」这层意思在英语里保留下来，用来指辫子，而辫子确实像尾巴一样垂着。

intro.en: Queue is a French word built on the Latin word for tail, and its journey from tail to waiting line explains most of its senses.
intro.cn: queue 是法语词，建立在拉丁语表示「尾巴」的词上；从尾巴到队伍这段路程解释了它的大部分义项。

items.en: Cauda meant the tail of an animal, and it stands behind several words about things that trail behind.
items.cn: cauda 指动物的尾巴，它支撑着好几个表示「拖在后面之物」的词。

items.en: Old French cue meant a tail and also a line of people or vehicles waiting one behind another.
items.cn: 古法语 cue 既指尾巴，也指人或车辆一辆接一辆等候的行列。

items.en: The later French spelling queue carried both the tail and the waiting-line senses across the Channel.
items.cn: 较晚的法语拼写 queue 把「尾巴」与「等候行列」两层意思一起带过了海峡。

items.en: English took the word for the waiting line, kept the old tail sense for a plait of hair, and later applied it to computer lists.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个词的「等候行列」义，保留「尾巴」义来指发辫，后来又把它用到计算机列表上。

items.en: Modern British English uses queue for almost any orderly line, while American English usually prefers line.
items.cn: 现代英式英语几乎用 queue 指任何有秩序的队伍，而美式英语通常更爱用 line。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same word and its close homophone; the near-meaning group gathers words for lines and waiting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的各种形式以及它的近音词；近义组收表示队伍与等待的词。

entries.definition: A signal that tells someone when to act or speak.
entries.definitionCN: 提示某人何时行动或说话的信号。

entries.definition: The act of standing in a queue.
A person who is waiting in a queue.
Someone who takes a place ahead of those already waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 越过已等候者抢先占位的人。

entries.definition: A row of people or things one behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个排成行的人或物。

entries.definition: A number of things arranged side by side.
A line of people moving one behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 一人接一人前进的行列。

entries.definition: To stay in place until something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 留在原地直到某事发生。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a tail and became a line of people, which is why a queue and an animal's tail share a picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从尾巴开始，变成了人群的行列，所以队列与动物尾巴共享同一幅画面。

normal.en: Queue and cue sound the same, but a cue tells you when to act while a queue is where you wait to act.
normal.cn: queue 与 cue 同音，但 cue 告诉你何时行动，queue 是你等待行动的地方。

normal.en: The silent letters after q are a reminder that the word came from French, where the tail still shows in the spelling.
normal.cn: q 后面那些不发音的字母提醒你这个词来自法语，尾巴的痕迹还留在拼写里。

normal.en: Queue up and join the queue describe the same act, one as a verb and one as a noun.
normal.cn: queue up 与 join the queue 描述同一个动作，一个用动词，一个用名词。

normal.en: A printer queue works first come, first served, exactly like a line of people at a window.
normal.cn: 打印机队列先到先处理，和窗口前排队的人一模一样。

normal.en: British speakers queue; American speakers usually stand in line.
normal.cn: 英国人用 queue，美国人通常说 stand in line。

abstract.en: A queue is a promise that order will be respected, and the promise is what makes waiting bearable.
abstract.cn: 队伍是一种「秩序会被尊重」的承诺，正是这个承诺让等待变得可以忍受。

abstract.en: Jumping the queue is a small act that reveals how much of society rests on strangers trusting a line.
abstract.cn: 插队这个小小的举动，暴露出社会有多少部分建立在对陌生人所排队伍的信任上。

abstract.en: To queue is to give up time now in exchange for a turn later, the plainest trade there is.
abstract.cn: 排队就是用现在的时间换将来的轮次，这是最朴素的一种交换。

examples.en: The queue for the concert stretched around the corner.
examples.cn: 音乐会的队伍拐过街角。

examples.en: We had to queue for nearly an hour.
examples.cn: 我们不得不排了将近一个小时的队。

examples.en: The print queue is empty, so the document should come out at once.
examples.cn: 打印队列是空的，所以文件应该会立刻打出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「Q」——队伍排得像一个大写的 Q，尾巴拖得长长的，记住 queue 是队伍、排队。

root: 拉丁语 cauda（尾巴）→ 古法语 cue（尾巴、行列）→ 法语 queue → 英语 queue；同族有 cue 的近音形式与 queueing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a tail-like line; the senses divide into the waiting line, the act of waiting, a computing list and an old plait of hair.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是像尾巴一样拖着的行列；义项分为等候的队伍、排队这一动作、计算机队列，以及旧时的长辫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line along a wall in the rain, umbrella tips touching.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中沿墙排开的长队，伞尖彼此相触。

branches.en: a rope of people down a wet street
branches.cn: 湿街上一条由人组成的绳索

branches.en: feet shifting slowly forward
branches.cn: 慢慢向前挪动的脚步

branches.en: a list fed in at one end
branches.cn: 从一端送入的清单

branches.en: a tail hanging down a back
branches.cn: 垂在背后的一条尾巴

branches.en: the same word for an animal's tail and a printer's list
branches.cn: 同一个词既指动物尾巴，也指打印机清单

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing whose Latin base means tail, with English endings that name the activity and the people involved.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语借词，其拉丁词基意为尾巴，再加上表示活动与参与者的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base cauda gave the French word its tail sense, and that single image holds the whole family together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 cauda 给法语词带来了尾巴义，就是这一个意象把整族词连在一起。

items.meaning: a list of waiting print jobs
